steps_raw.instruction: RNA Isolation and Reverse-transcriptase PCR

Before beginning RNA extraction, clean up the RNA room: change counter-top coverings and wipe everything with RNAase-zap or equivalent product. Use RNAase free plastic wear and rinse all glassware with RNAase-zap.
This protocol can be done at room temperature
The exact protocol will depend on the tissue type. Refer to the kit-specific instructions for more details:
Liver: http://www.qiagen.com/products/rnastabilizationpurification/rneasysystem/rneasymini.aspx#Tabs=t0
Muscle: http://www.qiagen.com/products/rnastabilizationpurification/rneasysystem/rneasyfibroustissuemini.aspx
RNA Isolation: Liver (quick guide to QIAGEN kit)
All steps to be done at room temperature, but do not allow frozen tissue to thaw before disruption in RLT buffer
Work quickly, but deliberately
Do NOT use bleach around these reagents
Buffer RLT may form a precipitate upon storage. If needed, re-dissolve by gently warming, then return to room temperature
Add 10 uL B-Mercaptoethanol (14.5M) per 1 mL RLT Buffer. Prepared buffer may be stored for up to 1 month at room temperature. Prepare and dispense buffer in fume hood.
Add 4 volumes 100% ETOH to buffer RPE before first use.

Obtain 20 mg pieces of liver tissue and place into bead beater tubes (BioSpec Products, Inc., Oklahoma, USA) containing 0.7mm zirconia beads (BioSpec Products, fill tubes ~1/4 to ~1/3 full). Keep on dry ice until ready to begin procedure.
Add 600 uL prepared RLT buffer to each tube, and secure the lids TIGHTLY.
Homogenize tissue in bead beater (Mini Beadbeater 16, BioSpec) for 1 minute, rest, then another minute. Ensure good tissue disruption.
Centrifuge samples for 3 minutes at full speed (in the bead beater tube)
Remove 500 uL of supernatant in to clean Eppendorf tubes. Avoid pipetting beads or other debris with the supernatant. Discard bead beater tubes.
Add 500 uL 50% ETOH to the cleared lysate and mix by pipetting.
Transfer up to 700 uL of sample to an RNeasy spin column, placed inside a 2 mL collection tube.
Close the lid and centrifuge for 15 seconds at 10,000xg
Discard the flow-thorough, and repeat for remaining lysate
Discard the flow-through
Add 700 uL buffer RW1 to the spin column. Centrifuge 15 seconds at 10,000xg
Discard the flow-through
Add 500 uL buffer RPE to the spin column. Centrifuge 15 seconds at 10,000xg
Discard the flow-through
Add 500 uL buffer RPE to the spin column. Centrifuge 2 minutes at 10,000xg
Replace collection tube with a clean one
Centrifuge 1 minute at full speed
Discard collection tube and flow-through
Place spin column in clean, labelled Eppendorf
Add 50 uL RNase-free water to spin column membrane (do not disturb membrane)
Centrifuge 1 minute at 10,000xg
Remove the eluate from the collection tube and replace into spin column, replace spin column into collection tube
Centrifuge once more for 1 minute at 10,000xg.
Quantify RNA via spectrophotometric determination of absorbance at 260 nm (Epoch plate reader with Take3 microplate, BioTek, Vermont, USA)
Evaluate purity via spectrophotometric determination of absorbance at 260 nm divided by absorbance at 280 nm (BioTek)
RNA Isolation: Muscle (quick guide to QIAGEN kit)
All steps to be done at room temperature, but do not allow frozen tissue to thaw before disruption in RLT buffer
Work quickly, but deliberately
Do NOT use bleach around these reagents
Buffer RLT may form a precipitate upon storage. If needed, re-dissolve by gently warming, then return to room temperature
Add 10 uL B-Mercaptoethanol (14.5M) per 1 mL RLT Buffer. Prepared buffer may be stored for up to 1 month at room temperature. Prepare and dispense buffer in fume hood.
Add 4 volumes 100% ETOH to buffer RPE before first use.
Heat bead bath (Benchmark Iso-Block, Benchmark Scientific, New Jersey, USA) to 55°C

Obtain 20 mg pieces of muscle tissue and place into bead beater (BioSpec Products, Inc., Oklahoma, USA) tubes containing 0.7mm zirconia beads (BioSpec Products, fill tubes ~1/4 to ~1/3 full). Keep on dry ice until ready to begin procedure.
Add 300 uL prepared RLT buffer to each tube, and secure the lids TIGHTLY.
Homogenize tissue in bead beater (Mini Beadbeater 16, BioSpec) for 1 minute, rest, then another minute. Ensure good tissue disruption.
Add 590 uL RNase-free water and 10 uL Proteinase K to each tube. Mix. Incubate at 55°C for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge samples for 3 minutes at full speed (in the bead beater tube)
Remove 500 uL supernatant in to clean Eppendorf tubes. Avoid pipetting any of the beads or other debris with the supernatant. Discard bead beater tubes.
Add 250 uL of 100% ETOH to the cleared lysate and mix by pipetting.
Transfer up to 700 uL of sample to an RNeasy spin column, placed inside a 2 mL collection tube.
Close the lid and centrifuge for 15 seconds at 10,000xg
Discard the flow-thorough, and repeat for remaining lysate
Discard the flow-through
Add 350 uL buffer RW1 to the spin column. Centrifuge 15 seconds at 10,000xg
Discard the flow-through
Add 350 uL buffer RW1 to the spin column. Centrifuge 15 seconds at 10,000xg
Discard the flow-through
Add 500 uL buffer RPE to the spin column. Centrifuge 15 seconds at 10,000xg
Discard the flow-through
Add 500 uL buffer RPE to the spin column. Centrifuge 2 minutes at 10,000xg
Replace collection tube with a clean one
Centrifuge 1 minute at full speed
Discard collection tube and flow-through
Place spin column in clean, labelled Eppendorf
Add 50 uL RNase-free water to spin column membrane (do not disturb membrane)
Centrifuge 1 minute at 10,000xg
Remove the eluate from collection tube and replace into spin column, replace spin column into collection tube
Centrifuge once more for 1 minute at 10,000xg.
Quantify RNA via spectrophotometric determination of absorbance at 260 nm (Epoch plate reader with Take3 microplate, BioTek, Vermont, USA)
Evaluate purity via spectrophotometric determination of absorbance at 260 nm divided by absorbance at 280 nm (BioTek)
Perform this procedure on wet ice
Dilute RNA samples to a total volume of 1ug RNA in 10uL RNAase free H2O. Use PCR clean plastic ware.
Dilute each sample in triplicate (to make 3 batches of CDNA for each sample)
Pick a sample to use for the standard curve. Make an additional set of triplicates.
Make Master Mix (High Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit, Life Technologies, California, USA):
Calculate the total number of reactions (with 3 per sample)
Add a couple of extra reactions to account for pipetting loss
Add the following ingredients for each reaction:
2.0uL Reaction Buffer
2.0 uL 10X random primers
1.0 uL Reverse Transcriptase
4.2 uL RNAase free H2O
Put 10 uL of master mix into the tubes containing 10 uL diluted RNA. Mix by pipetting.
Flash spin samples, then load into thermal cycler (Eppendorf, Thermostat, Hamburg, Germany).
Run CDNA reactions as follows:
Step 1: 25°C for 10 minutes
Step 2: 37°C for 120 minutes
Step 3: 85°C for 5 minutes
Step 4: Hold at 4°C indefinitely
Reverse-transcription PCR
Prepare PCR mater mix (TaqMan, Applied Biosystems, California, USA):
Calculate the total number of reactions (with 2 per CDNA sample)
Add a couple extra reactions to account for pipetting loss
Make the master mix by combining the following in a separate tube:
10 uL TaqMan master mix
Pipette 19 uL of master mix into each well on the plate that will contain a sample, including the standard curve, but skipping the first two wells of the standard curve
Pipette 1 uL CDNA into each sample well. Run each CDNA sample in duplicate. Mix by pipetting.
Prepare the standard curve (in duplicate) using the CDNA sample you prepared for this purpose:
Load the first two wells of the standard curve with 100ng RNA:
10 uL TaqMan master mix
Load the next two wells of the standard curve with 50 ng RNA:
(should already contain 19 uL master mix)
In a separate tube make a 1:10 dilution from 50ng (1ul of 50ng into 9ul of H2O)
Load 1 uL into the next two wells of the standard curve
(should already contain 19 uL master mix)
Using the 5ng solution, prepare a 0.5ng stock:
In a separate tube make a 1:10 dilution from the 5ng stock you just made (1ul of 5ng into 9ul of H2O)
Load 1 uL onto the next two wells of the standard curve
(should already contain 19 uL master mix)
Load no template control
Load 1 uL RNAase free H2O into the last wells of the standard curve
(should already contain 19 uL master mix)
Use a plate sealing sticker to seal the plate
Centrifuge the plate briefly on a plate spinner
Load the plate into the RT-PCR instrument (Applied Biosystems, California, USA)
Perform the PCR reactions with the following conditions:
Step 1: Hold at 50°C for 2 minutes
Step 2: Hold at 95°C for 10 minutes
Step 3: Denature at 95°C for 15 seconds
Step 4: Anneal/Extend at 60°C for 1 minute
Repeat Steps 3 and 4 for 40 cycles
Reaction volume: 20 uL
File > New > Standard Curve
Add detector > Copy to plate
Highlight wells containing samples and select the detector to be used.
Set up standard to be used
Label the no template controls as “NTC”
Set up the rest of the standard curve as “Standard,” indicating the amount of RNA loaded, and label the samples.
Set up the rest of the plate as “Unknown”
Label the samples but not the quantities
Instrument>Standard>Volume:20ul>Real Time>Connect
After run is completed, analyze the results:
Select the whole plate

The threshold is in the logarithmic portion of the graph and that it matches the thresholds that pertain to the same detector. They should only be 0.2-0.3 units apart in order to normalize the plates.
The slope of the graph is around -3.3+10%; this reflects an efficiency of 100% +10%.
The RT-PCR program outputs the starting quantity of RNA for each well
Check that sample replicates match up well with each other and average all of the replicates for each sample
Divide each sample average of the target gene by the corresponding sample average of the housekeeping gene control
This is the normalized RNA content; use these values for all other calculations.
Calculate the mean and standard error for each treatment group
To calculate the fold change from control to treatment use the following equation:
Fold Change= (treatment)/(control)
Multiply by 100 to get the percent change
